rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the primary uncertainty is whether a standard multimodal pipeline (combining RNA and image features) can achieve strong validation accuracy, and what baseline level to expect. Config_003 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is a well-motivated baseline: it uses established, reliable encoders (PCA for RNA dimensionality reduction, ResNet-50 for images), a simple robust aggregation (avgpool), and a standard weighted fusion. Testing this first establishes a reference performance level for the multimodal approach, clarifies whether the multimodal combination is beneficial, and provides a concrete anchor from which subsequent experiments can systematically vary one component (e.g., encoder choice, fusion strategy, aggregation) to identify what drives improvements. This maximizes information gain for the remaining 9 experiments by defining the landscape around a central, reasonable configuration.

With only one completed experiment (config_003: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted → 0.639 acc), evidence is extremely sparse. The most critical architectural decision in a multimodal model is how the two modalities are combined. config_008 is a clean single-variable A/B test: it changes only the fusion method from weighted to concat while holding all other settings identical (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool). This directly clarifies whether a learned weighted combination or a simple concatenation (letting the downstream classifier learn the interaction) is more effective. Understanding the fusion strategy early is high-value because it is a binary choice that will inform all subsequent multimodal experiments, and a small improvement here compounds across the remaining 8 experiments. It is the best use of experiment 2 because it reduces the most fundamental uncertainty with minimal confounding.

Evidence: config_003 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieved the best accuracy so far (0.639), and config_008 confirmed weighted fusion > concat under the same setup. The RNA encoder (pca_n2000) is a simple linear projection and may underutilize the rich single-cell transcriptomic signal. Question: Does replacing PCA with the pretrained scgpt encoder (a learned generative model capturing cell-type biology) improve accuracy while keeping all other settings at their best-known values? Why: This is a single-variable change from the current best, directly testing the most impactful unexplored dimension (RNA encoder quality). If scgpt helps, it opens a productive family of configs (scgpt + various image encoders/aggregations) for the remaining 7 experiments; if it doesn't, we confirm PCA is sufficient and can pivot to image encoder or aggregation changes. With only 2 data points, this high-information experiment is the best use of experiment 3 to reduce uncertainty on a core design axis.

Evidence: config_003 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the best at 0.639 acc, and config_034 shows scgpt is far inferior to pca_n2000 (~0.11 gap). config_008 shows weighted fusion slightly beats concat. However, we have zero information about the image encoder axis—only resnet50 has been tested. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l (a larger, more expressive ViT) improve performance when paired with the best-known RNA encoder (pca_n2000), aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted)? config_051 is a clean single-variable change from config_003, isolating the image encoder effect. Rationale: With 6 experiments remaining, we need to resolve whether a stronger image backbone is worth pursuing, as this decision gates many downstream combinations (e.g., whether to pair vit_l with transformer aggregation or scvi_n200). Testing this major architectural axis early maximizes information gain per experiment.

Evidence: config_003 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the best at 0.639 acc, and weighted fusion clearly beats concat (0.639 vs 0.619), while pca_n2000 strongly beats scgpt (0.639 vs 0.525). The image encoder choice (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) makes negligible difference (0.639 vs 0.635). The one major untested dimension for the top configuration is aggregation: avgpool is the only option tried so far with this exact combination. Question: Does transformer aggregation improve over avgpool when paired with the best-performing encoder/fusion settings? This is the best use of the next experiment because it is a minimal, well-motivated extension of the current best result—changing only one variable (aggregation) to test whether a more expressive pooling mechanism can push accuracy above 0.639. With 5 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest direction with a clean ablation maximizes expected gain while keeping the search focused.

The current best (config_003, acc=0.639) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder with resnet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion. We have strong evidence that pca_n2000 beats scgpt (0.639 vs 0.525), avgpool beats transformer (0.639 vs 0.573), and weighted beats concat (0.639 vs 0.619), but scvi_n200 has never been tested in this optimal multimodal/multiprofile setup. Config_022 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping all other settings at their best-known values, making it a clean single-variable test. This is the most important remaining uncertainty: whether a learned generative RNA representation can match or exceed the simple PCA baseline. With 4 experiments left after this one, confirming or ruling out scvi_n200 is critical—if it performs competitively, it opens a new promising axis; if not, it consolidates our confidence in pca_n200 and lets us focus remaining budget on marginal gains (e.g., vit_l + weighted fusion at 0.635). This is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step.

The best result so far is config_022 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.678), which clearly outperforms all other tested configurations. The RNA encoder scvi_n200 is the dominant factor (0.678 vs 0.639 for pca_n2000 vs 0.525 for scgpt), and avgpool+weighted is the preferred aggregation/fusion pair. The key untested dimension for the scvi_n200 pipeline is the image encoder: with pca_n2000, swapping resnet50→imagenet_vit_l was roughly neutral (0.639 vs 0.635), but the interaction with the more expressive scvi_n200 representation is unknown. Config_048 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) directly tests whether a stronger image encoder synergizes with the top RNA encoder while keeping the proven avgpool+weighted settings. This is the most logical single-step extension of the current best configuration and the highest-value use of experiment 7, leaving 3 experiments to further refine the winning recipe.

The current best is config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706). The only prior evidence against concat fusion (config_008 vs config_003, 0.619 vs 0.639) was with pca_n2000 + resnet50, where the lower-dimensional PCA features and simpler CNN features may benefit more from learned weighting. With scvi_n200 producing rich learned embeddings and imagenet_vit_l producing high-dimensional attention-based features, concatenation may better preserve complementary information that weighted averaging could dilute. This is a clean single-variable test from the current best. If it underperforms, the remaining experiment can probe aggregation (config_016) or confirm the best. This is the highest-value use of experiment 8: it directly tests whether the top config can be improved along the most uncertain remaining axis (fusion type) while keeping all other proven-optimal components fixed.

The current best (config_050, acc=0.715) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat. The strongest evidence shows scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l are the best encoders, and concat ≥ weighted for fusion. The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation—which was 6.6% worse than avgpool with weaker encoders (pca_n2000+resnet50: 0.573 vs 0.639)—might behave differently with the much stronger scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l representations, potentially capturing richer cross-modal interactions. Config_016 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) directly tests this. If it succeeds, it opens a new direction for the final experiment (e.g., config_020 with concat). If it fails, it confirms avgpool is optimal and our best remains config_050. This is the highest-information experiment available: it resolves the last major untested architectural dimension under the strongest encoder pair, and the outcome meaningfully guides the final experiment choice.

The current best is config_016 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as image encoder, and transformer as aggregation. The one untested cell in this top-tier space is transformer + concat fusion (config_020). We know concat outperformed weighted under avgpool (0.7150 vs 0.7062), suggesting fusion method interacts with aggregation. Testing transformer + concat directly probes whether this interaction holds at the higher-performing aggregation setting, potentially exceeding 0.7250. As the final experiment, exploiting the most promising single-variable extension of the current best is the highest-expected-value choice over exploring weaker encoder combinations.
